failures.criterion: AC2 and the reviewer's round-2 finding — the exemption marker must be a comment's business, so that text which is not a shell comment cannot buy a pass for a vulnerable command on the same line. It can again when the line's quotes do not balance.
failures.evidence: Measured against the real gate at this head, in fixtures built as its own suite builds them: `echo "see # check-check-commands: allow docs && bunx biome check .` passes the gate (exit 0, nothing reported), and so does its single-quote twin — while the same line without the marker is reported, and the balanced-quote version (`echo "see # check-check-commands: allow docs" && bunx biome check .`) is reported, which is the round-2 case that is still green. The cause is in `split_comment` (.github/scripts/check-check-commands.sh:393-405): when the quotes do not balance the command is the whole line, but the comment — and so the marker — comes from a second scan that tracks only the other quote character, so a marker inside the unterminated quote is read as a comment the shell never has, and `judge` (:507-520) returns on it before the command is read at all. The code's own docstring says the opposite: 'the marker is read from the comment `split_comment` finds and from nowhere else, so a line that quotes the marker inside a string exempts nothing it goes on to run'. Red test: `marker-inside-an-unclosed-quote` and its apostrophe twin in .github/scripts/check-check-commands.test.sh, with the control a fix must not break (`echo don't # check-check-commands: allow …`, which names no pinned tool and must stay green). `PYTHONPATH=/legion/pytools .github/scripts/check-check-commands.test.sh` reports `Results: 175 passed, 4 failed`.
